rationale: No framework-specific adapters are documented. Integration is only possible indirectly: an official MCP server works with Claude or any MCP client, cloud browsers expose CDP URLs that Playwright/Puppeteer or your own agents can connect to, and the browser infrastructure is positioned as a 'remote browser for your own agents'. This generic plumbing could be wired into agent frameworks, but none of the named frameworks are mentioned. Missing for 10: documented adapters or integration guides for Claude Agent SDK, Vercel AI SDK, LangChain and CrewAI, plus independent corroboration of framework integration.

It describes the Cloud Agent and Browser APIs and the open-source Python library, so an agent can be pointed directly at machine-oriented docs. missing for 10: evidence of a fuller agent-oriented docs set (e.g. llms-full.txt or per-page markdown), a machine-readable OpenAPI spec (all probed paths 404), and independent corroboration of agents actually consuming the docs.

Browser Use is a browser-automation agent and remote-browser infrastructure. It runs tasks on websites and returns results; it does not store user data in the product. AI-generated insights and suggestions over a user's data held inside the product is an analytics/data-platform axis, so it is a category error here. Data-extraction tasks such as exporting followers to CSV are task outputs, not an in-product insights feature, so they do not make the axis applicable.

Browser Use Cloud lets you start agent runs through an API (`client.runs.create`) that execute remotely without supervision. You monitor them by polling `runs.events()`, and saved login profiles, automatic CAPTCHA solving and stealth browsers keep runs going without human input. A community user also reports running ongoing LinkedIn automation. However, the evidence only shows on-demand, API-triggered runs, not configurable automations: there is no scheduling, recurring triggers or completion notifications, and 2FA or unsolved CAPTCHAs still require a human checkpoint. Missing for 10: scheduled/recurring or event-triggered automations, webhook/push notifications on completion, fully unattended handling of 2FA, independent hands-on corroboration of long-running background operation.

Browser Use is itself a task-delegation agent: you give it a goal and get the result (runs.create("Find the top Hacker News story"), "Give a high-accuracy browser agent a goal and get the result"). Sessions carry multiple runs, events can be polled to monitor progress, and human checkpoints handle 2FA. Community users report delegating real tasks such as LinkedIn automation. Missing for 10: no evidence of a built-in conversational UI for delegating tasks inside the product, since delegation is shown only through the API/SDK and library.

Browser Use can be driven entirely from code without a UI. Cloud SDK calls such as `client.runs.create` run tasks on remote managed browsers, and progress is tracked by polling `runs.events()`. Results come back as JSON that can be validated client-side, and a Python library automates the web 'from your own code', all of which fits unattended scripted or CI use. missing for 10: explicit documentation of a headless mode or CI pipeline setup (e.g. GitHub Actions guide, secrets handling), independent hands-on reports of CI usage.
